story: On Earth, noctilucent or 'night-shining' clouds float 80 kilometers high in the upper atmosphere. Visible only in twilight when the ground is dark while high altitudes remain sunlit, these rare clouds are made of water ice condensing around meteoric dust or rocket exhaust. But in 2006, ESA's Mars Express spacecraft detected something even stranger over Mars. Using its SPICAM instrument to observe distant stars dimming behind the planet's edge, scientists discovered tenuous clouds floating 80 to 100 kilometers high—the highest clouds ever recorded above any planet. At extreme altitudes, these Martian clouds aren't made of water ice. Instead, carbon dioxide gas freezes around microscopic dust particles to form dry-ice clouds that glow long after sunset. This discovery revealed that Mars' upper atmosphere is denser than previously thought, altering how engineers design aerobraking maneuvers for landing future spacecraft.
angle: The highest clouds ever discovered on any planet float up to 100 kilometers above Mars—and unlike Earth's night-shining ice clouds, they are made of frozen carbon dioxide.
disputed: Origin of microscopic nucleation dust on Mars: attribute as either surface rock dust lifted by winds or meteor debris burning up in the atmosphere.
Connection between 1885 Earth NLC discovery and 1883 Krakatoa eruption: attribute as an early hypothesis that was disproven as the sole cause by Malzev in 1926.
Radar reflectivity metallic coating hypothesis on Earth: leave out controversial hypothesis regarding sodium/iron coatings on ice grains.
